characters.name: Stanley Griff
characters.description: The titular six-year-old boy who loves animals, always looking them up on theGreat Big Book of Everything(or, on occasion, the Internet) to solve his problems. Animal Lover: Stanley loves all kinds of animals, looking towards them to solve whatever problems he has. Charlie Brown Baldness: He has only six strands on hair sticking outward, three on each side of his head.

characters.name: Lionel Griff
characters.description: Stanley's eleven-year-old older brother who loves rock music to the point of wearing headphones all the time. Big Brother Bully: He's more antagonistic to his younger brother in earlier episodes, most notably in "Kangaroo Clean-Up" (the second segment of the show's first episode) where he tries adding toys to Stanley's mess to prevent him from completing his room cleaning,thus missing dessert. Charlie Brown Baldness: He only has six strands of red hair sticking outward, much like his brother. However, he has four strands on his right side and two on his left.

characters.name: Mark Griff
characters.description: Stanley and Lionel's father, who is a stay-at-home cartoonist.

characters.name: Joyce Griff
characters.description: Stanley and Lionel's mother, who is a dentist.

characters.name: Dennis
characters.description: Stanley's pet goldfish and best friend, who teaches Stanley about animals as they explore the Great Big Book of Everything. Just don't sing that song to him when anybody mentions the book. Character's Most Hated Song: Woe be it to Dennis that he has to put up with Harry and Elsie singing theGreat Big Book of Everythingsong every time Stanley brings it out. Talking Animal: A goldfish who, despite being owned by Americans, inexplicably speaks with an Estuary English accent.

characters.name: Harry and Elsie
characters.description: Stanley's pet dog and cat, respectively. Harry likes to eat, Elsie often purrs when she starts speaking, and they both enjoy napping and singing the Great Big Book of Everything song (and its online version), the last of which is much to Dennis's annoyance. Running Gag: Mention theGreat Big Book of Everything, bring it out, or even justalludeto it, and theywillsing the book's theme song. Looking up something online with a computer instead? They have an "online" version of the song, too. Talking Animal: They sing, too, much to a fellow talking animal's chagrin. Verbal Tic:Harry often adds "dude" somewhere in his sentences, usually at the end.Elsie often purrs when she begins to speak. Harry often adds "dude" somewhere in his sentences, usually at the end.

characters.name: Lester Goldberg
characters.description: A Jewish boy who is one of Stanley's friends. Catchphrase: "Boy, oh boy!" Charlie Brown Baldness: He has only four strands of hair swooped down over his forehead. Informed Judaism: The episode "Little Dog Lost" has him mention that he celebrates Hanukkah instead of Christmas, revealing him to be Jewish.

characters.name: Marci and Mimi
characters.description: African American twin sisters who are friends of Stanley. Tomboy and Girly Girl: Marci has her hair in a bun and likes to play sports, with her overalls showing the print of a baseball on it. Mimi's hair is braided, accented by a purple bow, and her overalls has the print of a pink flower on it, reflecting her love of flowers.

characters.name: Jane
characters.description: A Chinese American girl in Stanley's class.
